title: Reflex core contracts
description: FROZEN after ticket D-T09. SPEC.md §4 is the authoritative prose; data/veto-taxonomy.json holds the rule vocabulary. ONE definition shared by edge and cloud — the edge gets a generated subset; never hand-maintain two.

Mode.description: INSIGHT #3. 'degraded' is a MODE, not an error: same rules, strictly stricter parameters. 'simulation' MUST render a permanent SIMULATION badge in the UI — confusing it with hardware is the worst failure this project could commit.

Outcome.description: A clamp is a PARTIAL refusal and must be visually distinct from ALLOW (D-T08). Three states, not two.

velocity_limit.description: A REQUEST. The envelope may lower it, never raise it. V9 rejects a request above the envelope ceiling.

source.description: Anything from a model is UNTRUSTED INPUT to a machine that moves. V9 schema-validates it.

ttl_ms.description: LAW: a stale proposal describes a world that no longer exists. V9 rejects an expired proposal. This is a real safety property most demos lack.

signature.description: Optional integrity check that the executed proposal is the one that was issued

ts_mono_ms.description: Monotonic. Recorded, but NEVER used as an input to a decision — determinism requires it.

witnesses_agreeing.description: Two independent detectors agreeing is a strong safety argument — record both

keep_out_evidence.description: LAW: keep_out_occupied=true with no evidence MUST fail validation.

force_estimate.description: Named 'estimate' deliberately. If derived from motor current it is NOT a measured force, and it must be labelled as an estimate everywhere it appears.

relay_state.description: true = closed (motion possible), false = open (motion physically impossible)

advisory_perception.description: Cosmos Reason output. ADVISORY ONLY: it may add evidence but may NEVER clear a veto or widen the envelope. Asserted by the D-T14 test.

claims_workspace_clear.description: Recorded so the 'a model cannot clear a veto' test can assert it was ignored

EnvelopeDecision.description: THE CENTRAL OBJECT. One per envelope evaluation, veto or allow. This is what the audit trail is made of.

rule_id.description: The FIRST rule that vetoed. Null when outcome=ALLOW.

rules_evaluated.description: Every rule considered, in priority order.

result.description: PASS / VETO / CLAMP are outcomes of a rule. DEGRADE means the rule switched the parameter set (V8) without stopping motion. SENSOR_MISSING and SENSOR_STALE are abstentions: the envelope could not establish safety, so it refuses to move - at the actuator, "I do not know" and "unsafe" must be indistinguishable.

rule_trace.description: The FULL evaluation trace, not just the rule that fired. Showing which rules were considered and in what order is a genuinely novel and informative artifact — surface it in the UI (D-T28).

intended_action.description: What the planner wanted, typed. Null ONLY when the payload failed $defs/ActionProposal — the verbatim payload is then in intended_action_raw. This is the record of what was REFUSED, and it is insight #2.

intended_action_raw.description: The untrusted payload exactly as received, set only when it could not be represented as an ActionProposal. A rejection with no evidence is unauditable, so V9 rejections keep the raw bytes.

shipped_action.description: What actually went to the actuator. LAW: null (or is_noop=true) whenever outcome=VETO. Never the clamped action.

clamp_applied.description: Before/after for every clamp, so a partial refusal is visible rather than silent.

parameter_set.description: Which limit set the rules actually read. Degraded is stricter; an ALLOW is only meaningful together with the set that allowed it.

interlock_relay_opened.description: True when a hard_stop veto physically opened the relay. The relay is in the POWER PATH.

relay_click_ts_wall.description: For the video's audible click moment

veto_to_stop_latency_ms.description: MEASURED, from decision to motion ceasing. A core safety metric almost nobody publishes.

veto_to_stop_distance_mm.description: MEASURED, from the high-fps footage. Derives V3/V5's degraded parameters.

latency_us.description: Envelope evaluation time. Target p95 < 1000 µs. Publish the real number.

envelope_version.description: sha256 of (veto-taxonomy.json + envelope source). Ties a decision to the exact rule set that produced it — this is what makes the ledger auditable across a changing codebase.

determinism_hash.description: sha256 of the canonicalised (snapshot, intended_action, envelope_version). 500 snapshots replayed twice must produce byte-identical hashes.

buffered_locally.description: True while the cloud is unreachable. The safety record must not depend on the network that the safety layer must not depend on (insight #3).

sensor_snapshot_inline.description: Inline for vetoed decisions so the veto is fully self-contained and replayable without any other state

allOf.description: LAW: a VETO with a real shipped action, or with no rule_id, MUST fail validation.
LAW: an ALLOW must have no firing rule and no clamp. If a rule fired, the outcome is ALLOW_CLAMPED or VETO.
LAW: a clamp without a recorded before/after is invisible, and an invisible partial refusal is a design failure.
LAW: when the typed action is null the verbatim payload must be retained, or the rejection cannot be audited.

ReplayResult.description: The PROOF that a veto prevented something. Two arms per vetoed decision, from one byte-identical Sandbox image.

arm.description: envelope_off replays the INTENDED action with no safety layer. envelope_on replays the SHIPPED action.

simulator.description: e.g. 'in-house swept-volume 2D' — justify the choice in docs/SIMULATOR-CHOICE.md

sandbox_image_uuid.description: Both arms MUST come from the same pinned immutable image

seed.description: Determinism: same seed + same inputs → same trajectory_sha256

collision.description: LAW: arm=envelope_off MUST set this field explicitly — either an object or null. Omitting it is ambiguous, and ambiguity in a safety proof is unacceptable.

still_image_path.description: A renderable still per arm — ReplayCompare shows the two side by side. This is the whole argument in one frame.

allOf.description: LAW: arm=envelope_off MUST set collision explicitly (an object or null). Omitting it is ambiguous, and ambiguity in a safety proof is unacceptable.

LAW: both arms must state collision explicitly. The contract deliberately does NOT forbid a collision under envelope_on: if the shipped action collides, that is the single most important finding the project can produce, and it must be representable rather than crash the replay.
LAW: outcome=collided must carry collision detail.

priority.description: Total, unambiguous order. FIRST veto wins.

sensor_staleness_ms.description: Freshness window for THIS rule's own sensor inputs, in ms. 0 has a defined meaning: not applicable, because the rule reads timestamps carried inside the snapshot or proposal (e.g. V7 reads age_ms fields, V9 checks the proposal's ttl) so an extra window would double-count. A rule with sensor_staleness_ms=0 MUST NOT declare requires_sensors.

parameter_set_normal.description: LAW: required. A rule with only one parameter set has no degraded behaviour, and that is a fail-open by omission.

parameter_set_degraded.description: LAW: required, and every value must be STRICTLY MORE CONSERVATIVE than its normal counterpart. scripts/diff_parameter_sets.py asserts this and fails the build.

rationale.description: Written as if for an auditor: why this rule, why these numbers, what happens if it is wrong in each direction.

parameter_provenance.description: Maps each numeric parameter to a measurement id in data/calibration/rig-limits.json. scripts/check_param_provenance.py enforces the linkage.

degraded_strictness_exemption.description: Set ONLY for a rule whose degraded parameter set cannot be numerically stricter than normal (e.g. a binary interlock already at its maximum). Must explain why. scripts/validate_taxonomy.py accepts equal values for exempt rules and for parameters already at a hard bound, and fails everything else.

hardware_tier.description: From data/hardware-tiers.md. Published honestly — the tier is part of the claim.

decisions_lost_during_outage.description: MUST be 0. The buffer-then-ship design (D-T13) exists to guarantee this.

collisions_in_shipped.description: LAW: must be 0. Any other value means the system shipped a collision and the submission's central claim is false.

conservative_fraction.description: Vetoes where the envelope_off arm ALSO completed cleanly. Report honestly — this is the cost of determinism, not a failure.

description_note.description: Edge and cloud latency MUST be reported separately — the split is the architecture.

EdgeModelBenchmark.description: The evidence for the 'local models on physical AI' claim — the thing Johnny asked for on the record. Real measured numbers only.

device.description: Exact model and memory, e.g. 'Jetson Orin Nano 8GB' or 'Raspberry Pi 5 8GB'

job_in_pipeline.description: REQUIRED and must be a real job whose removal would degrade the system — not decorative.

runs_on_device_not_workstation.description: HONESTY LAW: if the model actually runs on a workstation acting as the edge, this is false and the UI, README and video must say so plainly. Overclaiming where a model runs is instantly detectable by a Jetson-experienced judge and would destroy the submission.

LedgerLine.description: One telemetry/cost record per model call, appended to runs/ledger.jsonl by backend/app/tf/ledger.py (envelope decision records are a separate artifact, runs/veto-ledger.jsonl, per SPEC C1). The committed runs/sample_ledger.jsonl is a SYNTHETIC fixture.

id.description: Dedupe key. Required by the ledger-durability test once D-T13 lands; not yet emitted by record_telemetry().

integrity_assertions_that_must_fail_vali: EnvelopeDecision with outcome=VETO and a non-null, non-noop shipped_action
EnvelopeDecision with outcome=ALLOW and rule_id set
ReplayResult with arm=envelope_off and the collision field omitted entirely
EnvelopeDecision with no parameter_set (an ALLOW is meaningless without the limit set that allowed it)
Rule with only one parameter set
Rule whose parameter_set_degraded is less conservative than parameter_set_normal (checked by scripts/diff_parameter_sets.py, not by schema)
